newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH drops on possible KKR bid for DFS.
newsitem.headline: LVMH drops on possible KKR bid for DFS.

text.p: Shares in luxury group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton fell sharply on Friday in a higher market on fears of a bidding war for DFS in the U.S.
According to the Wall Street Journal, U.S. investment bank Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co was interested in making a rival bid for DFS Group Ltd.
"If it's going to be a war it could cost LVMH a lot of money," a dealer said.
At 0940 GMT, LVMH was down 1.34 percent at 1,247 francs.
LVMH on October 30 said it planned to buy the U.S. duty free chain for 12.6 billion francs to boost its presence along the affluent Pacific rim and extending control over its sales.

LVMH has agreed to buy 59 percent of San Francisco-based DFS but the deal is conditional on certain conditions. Industry soruces have said that one of the owners of DFS, billionaire Robert Miller, is blocking the sale of a stake by his partners because this would violate the terms of a 1991 agreement.
The Wall Street Journal, U.S. edition, said that KKR had approached the four controlling DFS shareholders and said it was interested in submitting a bid.
